description_ru: Юмористическая сцена в офисе фэнтези-королевства: менеджер по персоналу проводит ежегодную аттестацию дракона, охраняющего сокровища.
text:
The meeting was scheduled for ten o'clock in the Cavern of Eternal Flame, a venue chosen by Human Resources because, as Gwendolyn Pratt of People and Culture explained, it was "a safe space with excellent natural acoustics." She arrived at five minutes to the hour, carrying a laptop, a folder marked CONFIDENTIAL and a fire blanket, which she had been advised to bring by a colleague who had since taken early retirement. The dragon, whose name was Smaug-Dunmore the Third, was already waiting, coiled upon a hill of gold with the benign and watchful serenity of a very large cat.

"Gwendolyn," he said, in a voice like a landslide that had been taught elocution. "How delightful. Do take a seat. Mind the diadem." She sat, with some care, on a throne that had been designed for a person of far greater consequence, and opened her laptop. "Thank you for making time, Smaug," she said, with the brightness of a woman who has attended three workshops on difficult conversations. "This is just an informal chat about your annual performance review. There is absolutely nothing to be worried about." The dragon's left eye, the size of a dinner plate, narrowed slightly. A faint wisp of smoke curled from his nostril.

"Let's begin with the positives," she continued, consulting the screen. "Your core responsibility, the safeguarding of the treasure, has been fulfilled to a very high standard. You've retained one hundred percent of the hoard, with zero losses to theft, and in the past twelve months you've seen off eleven knights, four wizards and a travelling salesman." "The salesman was most persistent," observed the dragon. "I considered him a delicate matter." "Yes, we have noted that. Nobody has asked for the details." She cleared her throat. "Moving on. Your fire-breathing metrics are excellent."

"I am pleased," said Smaug-Dunmore. "I have always taken a certain pride in the fire." "You should," said Gwendolyn. "It is, as we say in the business, a standout deliverable. Which brings me, if I may, to some areas for development." A silence fell, so complete that she could hear a single coin sliding down the hill of gold. "We have received a number of comments from stakeholders," she said, in the tone of someone defusing a bomb. "Primarily from the neighbouring village. They have expressed a few concerns about your, um, approach to collaboration."

"The villagers," said the dragon, slowly, "have been burned." "Well, that's one way of putting it." "I mean this literally. I burned them. It was deliberate. I feel that it communicates an unambiguous message." Gwendolyn made a note. "I see. We'd like to reframe this as an opportunity. You see, our research suggests that stakeholders respond much better to feedback when it is delivered in a spirit of partnership, rather than, ah, incineration." "Is this the same research," enquired the dragon, "that recommended I should replace my sleeping hours with 'agile rest cycles'?" "That was a pilot," she said, a little hastily.

The review moved, with increasing awkwardness, to the question of communication style. Smaug-Dunmore, it appeared, had been issuing public announcements from the top of the mountain at all hours, in a roar that had cracked three windows and caused a lamentable incident among the cattle. "I need to emphasise," said Gwendolyn, "that roaring is not, under company guidelines, an appropriate form of broadcast. The preferred channel is email." "I do not have hands," said the dragon. "I have claws, and each of them is the size of a sword. I once attempted to type a message and destroyed a keyboard, a desk and a small but loyal intern."

Gwendolyn scribbled quickly. "I think we can classify that as an accessibility issue, and I will raise it with IT. Now. On teamwork." "I am alone in a mountain," said the dragon. "I have no team." "Exactly," said Gwendolyn, brightly. "We think there's an opportunity for greater cross-functional engagement. Perhaps a mentoring scheme with the Goblin Operations unit, or even a team-building day. Last year the trolls did an escape room and absolutely loved it." The dragon's gaze rested on her for a long moment. "I should enjoy that," he said, in a tone of such terrible courtesy that Gwendolyn adjusted her fire blanket.

At this point the conversation took an unexpectedly sincere turn. The dragon sighed, and the sigh moved the coins like a tide. "May I confide in you, Gwendolyn? For four hundred years I have kept this gold. I have defended it from the greedy and the brave. And in all that time, no one has once asked whether I wished to." The words hung in the air like soot. "You see, I have never actually spent any of it. I do not know what a coin is for. I lie upon it, I count it, and I am told that it is mine. But I should dearly like, just once, to buy a hat."

Gwendolyn looked at him for a while. She had expected a number of things from this review: threats, perhaps, or a modest degree of singeing. She had not expected pathos. She closed her laptop, and put aside her script, and when she spoke it was in the voice of a person rather than a department. "Smaug," she said, "I think we've been asking the wrong questions. What would you like your career to look like?" The dragon considered. "I think," he said, "I should like to consult. Perhaps in the field of risk management. I have, after all, considerable experience of being feared."

They talked for an hour. By the end, a new development plan had been drawn up: a secondment to the Kingdom's Treasury, a part-time role advising on the security of vaults, and a modest allowance for hats. The dragon, in a moment of unguarded joy, produced a long plume of flame, which ignited the folder marked CONFIDENTIAL, and Gwendolyn, who had anticipated this, smothered it with her blanket without breaking the flow of her sentence. It is a mark of true professionalism, she reflected afterwards, to be ready for a catastrophe and to avoid mentioning it.

Back in the office, her manager asked how it had gone. "Very constructive," she said, removing a singed eyebrow with a sigh. "He's a high performer with enormous potential, who needs, in my view, to be encouraged to explore a wider range of interests." "And the village?" "We shall approach it as a lessons-learned exercise." Her manager nodded. "Did he say anything about next year's targets?" Gwendolyn paused, and thought of the great gold hill, and the great eye, and the hat. "He said," she replied, "that he'd like to grow into the role."

Кончик языка между зубами, без голоса; не заменяйте на «с», «ф» или «т».
Дифтонг: начинайте с широкого «а», плавно уходите к «и»; в слове fire добавляется лёгкий ə.
Язык не касается нёба, губы слегка округлены; английское r мягче русского «р».

questions.question: Who is conducting the performance review?
questions.answer: Gwendolyn Pratt from Human Resources, People and Culture.
